record.what_it_does: Visual discovery platform; API for pins, boards, ads, analytics and catalogs.
record.auth_notes: OAuth 2.0 authorization code flow with scopes. Redirect URIs must exactly match the registered ones. Refresh tokens are continuous: they expire after 60 days and can be refreshed indefinitely. Pinterest also supports the OAuth Client Credentials grant (tokens prefixed pinc, 30-day lifetime) for an app acting on its own behalf. Only some endpoints accept those tokens, and Pinterest's own community FAQ contradicts this, so test it first. After Trial approval, you can generate short-lived test tokens (24h) without setting up OAuth. The app ID and secret are issued after Pinterest approves the app.
record.access_notes: Free, but Pinterest reviews each app request before issuing credentials. Approved apps get Trial access. Trial is rate limited per app per day, and Pins and Boards created on Trial are visible only to their creator as Sandbox entities. Offering the API to real users needs an upgrade to Standard access. The access-tiers page says the upgrade requires a video recording of the app using the API, including the OAuth flow. No turnaround time is published. No paid plan was found.
record.api_breadth_notes: API v5 covers pins, boards, user account, media, search, ad accounts, campaigns, ad groups, ads, audiences, catalogs, conversion events, lead ads, analytics and keywords. I did not count operations, but it is clearly over 50. A raw OpenAPI spec is published in Pinterest's api-description GitHub repo.
record.mcp_notes: developers.pinterest.com/about-pinterest-mcp/ shows https://api.pinterest.com/mcp (http transport, Bearer token, OAuth 2.0) in an example config. On re-check the page is still a pre-launch announcement ("Be the first to know when it launches", "Sign up for updates"), so the server is announced but not confirmed live. Several community MCP servers also exist.
record.blocker_notes: Pinterest must approve the app before it gets Trial access. Trial content lives in a creator-only sandbox and has daily per-app rate limits. A multi-user production toolkit needs the Standard upgrade, which is reviewed and requires a video demo of the OAuth flow. Webhooks exist only for lead ads.
